subject: Nanotechnology
title: Sodium-Ion Nano Batteries
description: A quick win: understand Sodium-Ion Nano Batteries.

hook.text: Sodium is 1000 times more abundant than lithium — nano electrodes make sodium-ion batteries finally competitive.

buildup.text: Sodium ions are larger than lithium — they need wider diffusion channels that nanostructured hosts provide.

discovery.text: Hard carbon nanospheres with tunable pore sizes intercalate sodium efficiently — reaching 300 mAh per gram.

twist.text: Sodium batteries are heavier per kWh than lithium — they suit stationary storage better than electric vehicles.

climax.text: CATL ships sodium-ion batteries for grid storage — nano-engineered electrodes make cheap abundant elements viable.

punchline.text: Nano channels in carbon welcome the bigger sodium ion — cheap energy storage arrives.

quiz.question: Why do sodium-ion batteries need nanostructured electrodes?
options: Sodium ions are smaller and need tighter confinement
Larger sodium ions require wider diffusion channels that nanostructured hosts provide
Sodium reacts violently with bulk materials
